findings.title: restartHub and the EnsureReady recordBoots wiring have no test
findings.body: Every new test replaces `p.replaceHub` with a fake, so `restartHub` never runs under test. It holds the real logic: `hub.cancel()`, the 5s wait on `hub.done`, clearing `p.hub`, `EnsureReady`, the `reviveHub` fallback on failure, and the `replacingHub` reset in the defer. A mistake there would leave `replacingHub` stuck at true, so no later outside boot would ever replace the hub, and no test would catch it. The goroutine in `EnsureReady` (line 254) that calls `recordBoots` is also untested: `TestHubStartRecordsEverySimulatorsBoot` calls `recordBoots` directly. A test with a stubbed `lookPath`/`startHub`, or one that drives `restartHub` with a fake hub whose `done` is closed, would cover both.

findings.title: Boot-recording tests are skipped off macOS because of the GOOS gate in unlistedSimulators
findings.body: `recordBoots` goes through `unlistedSimulators`, which returns early when `runtime.GOOS != "darwin"`. `TestOutsideBootAfterAnUnwatchedAOBootIsCaught`, `TestHubStartRecordsEverySimulatorsBoot` and `TestListCarriesSimulatorBoots` therefore skip on Linux CI, which is where most CI runs. The Boot-records-its-own-boot and hub-start-records-all-boots paths, which the PR is built around, are covered only on macOS runners. The tests could stay portable if the GOOS check were injectable. Alternatively, confirm that a macOS job runs this package.
